source.title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II

accepted.question_text: For the Korteweg–de Vries equation u_t + u u_x + u_xxx = 0 on the real line with almost periodic initial data u(x,0)=u_0(x), does the solution exist and evolve almost periodically in time whenever the spatial initial profile is almost periodic?

evidence.quote: This result leads to the following natural conjecture: The same is true if u0(x) is almost periodic, i.e., if the initial data is almost periodic in space, the solution evolves almost periodically in time.

accepted.question_text: For suitable perturbations of the Korteweg–de Vries equation and suitable almost periodic initial data u_0(x), does the Cauchy problem have a unique global solution u(x,t) that evolves almost periodically in time, in analogy with KAM-type persistence in finite-dimensional integrable systems?

evidence.quote: It is a natural, open and very challenging conjecture that the result of Damanik et al. remains true for (suitable) perturbations of KdV, i.e., for (suitable) perturbations of KdV, the Cauchy problem with (suitable) almost periodic initial data u0(x), has a unique global solution u(x, t), which evolves almost periodically in time.

accepted.question_text: For random n×n band matrices H with bandwidth w and independent entries inside the band, is the local eigenvalue statistics regime governed by a sharp transition at bandwidth about sqrt(n), with GUE-type statistics when w is much larger than sqrt(n) and Poisson statistics when w is much smaller than sqrt(n)?

evidence.quote: The long-standing conjecture of V. Fyodorov and A. Mirlin [59] from 1991 is that for iid Hij , |i − j| < w, with w ≫ √n, the local statistics of the eigenvalues of H are GUE, but for w ≪ √n, the behavior is Poisson.

accepted.question_text: For random Schrödinger operators H = -Δ + V in dimension d=3 with random potential V, are eigenfunctions delocalized in the bulk of the spectrum, do eigenvalues exhibit random-matrix statistics there, and does there exist a mobility edge μ separating Poisson statistics from random-matrix statistics?

evidence.quote: It is believed that in the bulk of the spectrum for d = 3, the eigenfunctions of H are delocalized and the eigenvalues exhibit random matrix statistics. There is also believed to be a so-called mobility edge µ in the spectrum at which the statistics switch from a Poisson distribution to a random matrix distribution. So far this conjecture is wide open.

accepted.question_text: Can one prove universality, both in the bulk and at every edge, for Wigner ensembles whose equilibrium measure is supported on more than one interval?

evidence.quote: Another open problem in RMT is to prove universality, in the bulk and at (all) the edges, for Wigner ensembles in the case that the equilibrium measure for the ensemble is supported on more than one interval.

accepted.question_text: For Wigner ensembles whose equilibrium measure changes topology as parameters vary, can one analyze and control the critical regimes where intervals in the support of the equilibrium measure open, close, or merge, including the associated local universality classes?

evidence.quote: Furthermore, one would like to analyze and control situations where parameters in the underlying matrix distributions vary, and intervals in the support of the equilibrium distribution for the ensemble open and close.

accepted.question_text: In random matrix models with external parameters p and critical values p_c where the equilibrium measure changes its nature, can one rigorously analyze the double-scaling regime p→p_c together with matrix size n→∞, and more generally the relevant multi-scaling limits?

evidence.quote: The double-scaling problems, p → pc and matrix size n → ∞, are of basic interest. Most of these problems remain open.

accepted.question_text: Can Rumanov’s explicit Painlevé-II-based description of the Tracy–Widom distribution for β=6 be made fully rigorous, and can the same program be carried out rigorously for all even β>0?

evidence.quote: It is of great interest to complete Rumanov’s analysis rigorously, not only for β = 6, but for all even β > 0.

accepted.question_text: Can the detailed asymptotic formulas proposed by Borot, Eynard, Majumdar, and Nadal for Tracy–Widom distributions of general β-ensembles be verified rigorously for all β>0?

evidence.quote: It is a challenging open problem to verify rigorously these formulae of Borot et al.

accepted.question_text: Is the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang equation itself in the KPZ universality class, in the sense that one can rigorously prove the characteristic 3:2:1 scaling between time, spatial correlations, and fluctuations for its solutions?

evidence.quote: A basic question is whether KPZ is in the KPZ universality class. In other words, can one show rigorously that solutions of KPZ indeed have the KPZ scaling 3 : 2 : 1?

accepted.question_text: For the Cauchy problem for the KPZ equation, can one prove strong 3:2:1 KPZ universality for a wide class of initial data and identify the limiting process predicted by physics?

evidence.quote: The most challenging open problem regarding the KPZ equation is to prove 3 : 2 : 1 KPZ universality in the strong sense of Corwin, Quastel and Remenik [30] alluded to above, for solutions of the Cauchy problem of the KPZ equation for a wide set of initial data, and to identify the limiting process.

accepted.question_text: Can one analyze solutions of the KPZ equation at more than one space-time point, rather than only single-point distributions or partial marginal information?

evidence.quote: Another open problem is to analyze solutions of KPZ at more than one space-time point.

accepted.question_text: Does last-passage percolation with general weight distributions exhibit the full 3:2:1 KPZ scaling, including the correct fluctuation and correlation exponents?

evidence.quote: In particular showing that LPP with general weights has 3 : 2 : 1 scaling, is far from being resolved.

accepted.question_text: For the longest increasing subsequence problem under non-uniform distributions on permutations or more general input distributions, do the fluctuations still satisfy KPZ-type universality, and how do those fluctuations behave?

evidence.quote: Also, regarding the original longest increasing subsequence problem, KPZ universality for the fluctuations has been proved so far only for the uniform distribution on the permutations: The problem for the fluctuations with more general distributions is very much open.

accepted.question_text: Can one explain conceptually how Tracy and Widom’s solution of ASEP works and extend that method to more general initial data for ASEP and related interacting-particle models?

evidence.quote: In another direction, it remains an open, and somewhat mysterious, problem to understand how Tracy and Widom’s solution of ASEP actually ‘works’, and to extend their method of solution to more general initial data.

accepted.question_text: Can one develop a perturbation theory for non-solvable KPZ and interacting-particle models analogous to KAM theory, so that one can study persistence of integrable structures and robustness of asymptotic scaling phenomena under perturbation?

evidence.quote: Developing such a perturbation theory is an open conceptual and technical problem of the first order.

accepted.question_text: To prove universality for the centered and scaled stopping-time variable associated with the Toda eigenvalue algorithm, can one control jointly, as n→∞, the statistics of the relevant extreme eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvector components for β=1 invariant ensembles and for β=1 or β=2 Wigner ensembles?

evidence.quote: In order to prove universality for the centered and scaled variable T(1)−⟨T(1)⟩/σT(1) ... for β = 1 invariant ensembles, and for β = 1 or 2 WE’s, this problem is still very much open.

accepted.question_text: For the QR eigenvalue algorithm on random matrices, can one determine the bulk statistics of eigenvalue ratios near zero together with the associated eigenvector information well enough to prove a universality theorem analogous to the Toda result?

evidence.quote: It is very much an open problem to control, as n → ∞, the statistics of |λj+1/λj|, |λj−1/λj| for λj ∼ 0 deep in the bulk of the spectrum, together with their associated normalized eigenvectors, as in (8), (9).

accepted.question_text: Can one prove an analog of the Toda stopping-time universality theorem for the full deflation time T_{ε,n,A,E} of some eigenvalue algorithm A, where deflation requires control of more of the eigenvector structure and not only the top eigen-gap?

evidence.quote: The most challenging problem for eigenvalue computation with random data is to prove the analog of Theorem 1 for the deflation time Tε,n,A,E ... for some algorithm A.

accepted.question_text: Can one rigorously prove universality for other random-data numerical algorithms discussed in the paper, such as the conjugate-gradient method for solving Ax=b with random A and random b?

evidence.quote: It is an interesting and challenging open problem to prove universality rigorously for any of the other numerical algorithms discussed in [40]. The conjugate gradient algorithm, in particular, to compute the solution of the linear system Ax = b with A and b random, seems to be ‘within reach’.

accepted.question_text: Can the high-accuracy orthogonal-polynomial-based sampling method for invariant unitary ensembles be extended to orthogonal and symplectic invariant ensembles?

evidence.quote: It is an open problem to extend the method of S. Olver et al. to orthogonal and symplectic invariant ensembles.

accepted.question_text: For the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the half-line x≥0 with prescribed initial data u(x,0)=f(x) and boundary forcing u(0,t)=e^{iwt}, can one compute the long-time asymptotic behavior of the solution u(x,t) as t→∞ for fixed real w?

evidence.quote: A particular stand out open problem is to compute the long-time behavior of the solution u(x, t) of the focusing NLS equation, iut = uxx + 2|u|2u, with u(x, 0) = f(x), x ≥ 0, given and u(0, t) = eiwt, t ≥ 0 with w ∈ R.

accepted.question_text: Can the Bikbaev–Tarasov Bäcklund-transform method be used to solve the initial-boundary value problem for the defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the half-line with Robin boundary conditions at x=0, while controlling the singularities introduced by the extension to x<0?

evidence.quote: It is an interesting open problem to use the Bikbaev–Tarasov method to solve the IBVP for defocusing NLS, iut = uxx − 2|u|2u, with Robin boundary conditions at x = 0.

accepted.question_text: For nonlinear Schrödinger initial-boundary value problems on the half-line with Robin boundary conditions and smooth, corner-compatible initial and boundary data, can one prove that the solution is a classical solution in x>0, t>0 for a general class of nonlinearities, rather than only in special integrable cases?

evidence.quote: So the open problem here is a PDE problem, viz., to prove that the IPVP for NLS with a general class of non-linearities, with Robin boundary conditions and matching, smooth initial data, is classical in x > 0, t > 0.

accepted.question_text: For focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equations in the small-dispersion regime ε=ℏ→0 and general smooth initial data, can one solve the non-self-adjoint forward scattering problem and then implement the associated Riemann–Hilbert method to compute the Cauchy problem asymptotically?

evidence.quote: It remains an open problem (see [34]) to solve the forward problem for focusing NLS with general smooth initial data, and then implement the RHP methodology, to obtain the solution of the Cauchy problem in the small dispersion limit ϵ = ℏ ↓ 0.

accepted.question_text: For the Airy integral operator acting on L²(s,∞), can one determine the asymptotic behavior of its eigenfunctions as s→∞ and compute those eigenfunctions accurately for finite s?

evidence.quote: It is an open problem to analyze the behavior of the eigenfunctions u˜j(s) as s → ∞, and to compute their behavior for finite s.

accepted.question_text: For perturbations of the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation of the form i u_t + u_xx + 2|u|²u + ε|u|^ℓ u = 0 with decaying initial data, especially when the unperturbed initial data produces a two-soliton solution, what is the long-time behavior of the perturbed solution?

evidence.quote: An open problem of great and basic interest is to analyze solutions of the Cauchy problem for perturbations of the focusing NLS equation ... Of particular interest is the case where f˜(x) corresponds to a 2-soliton solution for (unperturbed) focusing NLS.

accepted.question_text: Can one use Riemann–Hilbert and nonlinear steepest-descent methods to give a fully rigorous proof of the asymptotic binary-periodic behavior claimed for the Toda shock problem with exponential forces and supercritical drive?

evidence.quote: The first is to use Riemann–Hilbert/steepest-descent methods to prove the results in Venakides et al. rigorously.

accepted.question_text: If the exponential Toda interaction e^x is replaced by a general force law F(x) that is a sufficiently small perturbation of e^x and admits a suitable 2-periodic solution, does the corresponding shock problem still have the same long-time asymptotic behavior as the Toda shock problem, and how can that behavior be analyzed rigorously?

evidence.quote: Second open problem: Analyze the general shock problem (15) for suitably small perturbations F(x) of ex.

accepted.question_text: Can one give a rigorous and explicit mathematical solution of the fixed-frequency diffraction problem for two slits in the plane, the classical double-slit problem underlying Young’s experiment and its quantum-mechanical analogues?

evidence.quote: However the rigorous solution of the problem of diffraction from two slits remains open.
This is a problem of the first order, whose rigorous and explicit solution would generate great interest in the mathematical and physics communities.
